headline: Dry autumn sunshine prevails; Kentucky valleys stay chilly with patchy frost and fog while a cool, breezy Upstate wedge deepens this weekend
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: Clear, chilly dawn conditions around Danville give way to a sunny Friday and a steady weekend warm-up. High pressure keeps the full 72-hour period dry. The only local concerns are patchy valley fog and frost during the coldest pre-dawn hours, while afternoons climb from near 70 today into the lower 70s this weekend.
kentucky.currentConditions: At 4:15 AM EDT, KDVK was clear at 39°F with a 36°F dew point, calm wind and 10-mile visibility. At 4:45 AM, KLEX was partly cloudy at 45°F with a 39°F dew point, a light east-northeast wind and 10-mile visibility. No precipitation or official alert was present at issuance.

days.label: Friday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for the Danville point. Independent concern is limited to patchy frost and localized valley fog late tonight into early Saturday; a widespread freeze is not expected.
days.forecast: Sunny after daybreak with a light east breeze around 2–7 mph. Danville's most likely high is 69°F. Tonight turns clear and chilly; the most likely Danville low is near 40°F, while sheltered rural valleys may briefly reach the middle to upper 30s with patchy frost or fog.

days.label: Saturday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for Saturday at issuance. Patchy valley fog or frost is possible around daybreak Sunday, but no widespread hazardous weather is expected.
days.forecast: Any isolated valley fog or frost dissipates quickly, followed by full sunshine and a very light east wind. Danville's most likely high is 72°F. Saturday night remains mostly clear, with a most likely Danville low near 41°F and a few colder valleys in the upper 30s.

days.label: Sunday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for Sunday at issuance, and no significant independent hazard is expected. Localized pre-dawn valley fog remains a low-probability concern.
days.forecast: Sunny and pleasantly mild with a light east wind. Danville's most likely high is 73°F. Sunday night stays clear and cool with a most likely low near 42°F; patchy fog may form in the most sheltered river valleys toward Monday morning.

kentucky.bottomLine: Central Kentucky stays dry and sunny through Sunday. Most likely Danville highs are 69°F, 72°F and 73°F; most likely nighttime lows are 40°F, 41°F and 42°F. Patchy frost or valley fog is possible near daybreak, but no official alert is active.
kentucky.confidence: High on dry weather and afternoon temperatures; moderate-high on exact valley lows and localized frost or fog placement

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson primary · Central/Pickens County comparison
upstate.summary: A clear Friday gives way to a stronger dry northeast-flow wedge this weekend. The entire 72-hour period remains rain-free, but Saturday and Sunday turn cooler and breezier. Clemson stays several degrees milder at night than sheltered Central and Pickens County locations.
upstate.currentConditions: At 4:40 AM EDT, KCEU was clear at 54°F with a 43°F dew point, north wind near 6 mph and 10-mile visibility. At 4:15 AM, KLQK was clear near 42°F with a 40°F dew point, calm wind and 10-mile visibility. The roughly 12°F station spread confirms the established nighttime microclimate difference; Tempest data was not used.

days.label: Friday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for the Clemson point. No significant independent weather hazard is expected today or tonight.
days.forecast: Sunny and dry with a light northeast wind around 3–8 mph. Clemson's most likely high is 69°F. Tonight is mostly clear; the most likely Clemson low is near 46°F, while sheltered Central and Pickens County locations may fall near 40°F.

days.label: Saturday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for Saturday at issuance. The independent concern is a breezy northeast wind with gusts around 18–25 mph; no freeze or widespread frost is expected in the Clemson–Central corridor.
days.forecast: Sunny but cooler as a strong, dry wedge becomes established. Clemson's most likely high is 66°F. Northeast wind runs 8–13 mph with gusts near 18–25 mph. Saturday night stays clear and breezy; Clemson is most likely near 43°F, with sheltered Central locations in the upper 30s.

days.label: Sunday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for Sunday at issuance. Breezy northeast flow remains the independent concern, with gusts around 18–25 mph but below advisory criteria.
days.forecast: Sunny, cool and still breezy beneath the persistent dry wedge. Clemson's most likely high is 66°F. Northeast wind runs 7–12 mph with gusts near 18–25 mph. Sunday night remains clear; Clemson is most likely near 43°F while sheltered Central locations fall into the upper 30s.

upstate.bottomLine: The Clemson–Central corridor remains sunny and dry through Sunday. Most likely Clemson highs are 69°F, 66°F and 66°F; most likely Clemson lows are 46°F, 43°F and 43°F, with sheltered Central locations several degrees colder. Breezy northeast flow is the only notable weekend concern.
upstate.confidence: High on dry weather; moderate-high on weekend highs because the older NAM is colder than the newer guidance cluster

analysisLinks.label: College of DuPage satellite and radar

sourceNotes: No official NWS alert was active for either configured point when the alert APIs were checked at 5:00 AM EDT. Official alerts remain separate from this independent analysis.

NWS discussions and point forecasts, HRRR, RAP, NAM, NAM 3-km, GFS, GEFS and ECMWF agree on a dry 72-hour period. The older 00Z NAM is roughly 3–8°F colder than the GFS and ECMWF benchmarks for the Upstate weekend, so it defines the cool edge rather than the most likely value; this is a manageable uncertainty, not a material unresolved conflict.

Local BUFKIT 19 was used to inspect the underlying KLEX NAM, HRRR, RAP and GFS profiles; current KGSP profile files came from the BUFKIT Warehouse. KLEX profiles showed a dry column, shallow nighttime inversions and light east flow; KGSP profiles supported a dry northeast-flow wedge. BUFKIT was not counted as a separate model.

The 8:55 AM UTC College of DuPage Ohio Valley radar showed no coherent precipitation near central Kentucky; scattered weak returns were consistent with clutter. The 9:01 AM UTC infrared frame showed only thin or scattered cloud texture, with no organized deep cloud shield over the target area.

College of DuPage Southeast radar at 8:55 AM UTC showed no coherent precipitation near the Upstate, and clean-infrared satellite at 8:56 AM UTC showed the Carolinas largely clear with organized cloudiness offshore.

Chris Bailey's October 23 Kentucky Weather Center post described the dry, pleasant pattern continuing through the weekend and much of next week; its more active Halloween signal lies beyond this 72-hour forecast.

The latest cumulative accuracy summary was consulted: 26 verified forecasts, 70 verified checkpoints and 74.1% all-category accuracy. Station corrections, empirical range widths, regime-specific model weights, fog timing and official-alert handling were applied.

Temperature cards retain calibrated regional coverage ranges, while the prose supplies the narrower most-likely Danville and Clemson values requested by the user. Wider nighttime ranges are retained because KCEU and KLQK differed by about 12°F at issuance and Kentucky valleys remain colder than exposed sites.
Tempest data was not used for Upstate observations, verification, calibration or adjustment.
